question: At what rate spread does a refinance pay back its closing costs?
thesis: most calculators divide the bill by the monthly saving; counting what is still owed on each loan, break-even comes later for a loan that is already some years old

median.what: ILLUSTRATIVE: borrowed 2023-10 at that month's mean rate (7.62%), 35 payments made; loan $375,000, bill $5,123.53 = HMDA 2025 median rate-and-term refinance (all sizes)

small.what: ILLUSTRATIVE: borrowed 2023-10 at that month's mean rate (7.62%), 35 payments made; loan $115,000, bill $3,667.05 = HMDA 2025 median, loans under $150,000

large.what: ILLUSTRATIVE: borrowed 2023-10 at that month's mean rate (7.62%), 35 payments made; loan $655,000, bill $5,513.97 = HMDA 2025 median, conforming (flag C) loans of $600,000 to under $720,000

hold36.what: sell or refinance again after 3 years (36 months): the payback target of the question
hold36.wordsFrom: story/script-v3.2.md: "a stay of three years" (S08), "after three years" (S16, S17, S20), "the three-year test" (S13)

assumptions.pattern: matches the national average|national average rate
assumptions.what: the offered rate = the national weekly average (MORTGAGE30US) of the date anchor
closing costs are paid in cash, not added to the loan
worth it = fees paid back within 3 years (analyst choice)
the old loan was taken out at the October 2023 average rate
the bill is the HMDA 2025 median for the loan size
the new loan is a fresh 30-year fixed loan

paramsFrom.oldRate: mean of the weekly MORTGAGE30US values dated October 2023 (claim r_old)
paramsFrom.paymentsMade: months from 2023-10 to the date anchor month (claim k35)
paramsFrom.notModel: metadata copied into model.json, not computed: date anchor text, the large band label, FHFA limits (data/cll.json)

recompute: payment = P*r/(1-(1+r)^-n), r = annual%/1200; old loan P0 at r_old over 360 with k payments made; balance B = balance after k; new loan B at r_new over 360
MAIN break-even (counting what is still owed): first month m with (payment_old - payment_new) x m + (balance_old(k+m) - balance_new(m)) >= C
simple break-even (shown as the contrast): ceil(C / (payment_old - payment_new))

history: monthly means of MORTGAGE30US; drop episodes = zig-zag swings >= 1.00 point; refinance in the first month >= spread under the peak; cost = HMDA median share of that year (fixed median share before 2018, ILLUSTRATIVE)

crosscheck.what: Freddie Mac PMMS weekly (MORTGAGE30US) vs the mean of the Optimal Blue daily rates (OBMMIC30YF) of the 7 days ending that Thursday, every week since 2017-01-06
